title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction: This is the opening page of the third draft ('troisième mouture', 23 June 1986) of Grothendieck's chapter on 'Analysis situs'. It belongs to his post-Esquisse attempt to found 'tame topology' (topologie modérée) axiomatically. He states the plan: to recapitulate the data and axioms of an 'algebra of figures', which he also calls an 'atelier' (workshop). For now he wants only the purely algebraic axioms, that is, the lattice- or Boolean-type formalism governing how figures combine. He explicitly postpones three kinds of property: (i) topological properties of figures (density or dimension, connectedness, acyclicity); (ii) properly geometric properties (topological regularity, and what counts as a topological ball or sphere inside an algebra of figures); (iii) 'finite combinatorial properties' centred on the notion of complex. Among the axioms he singles out a core group At 1–At 7. He regards these as essential for giving the formalism its geometric-topological meaning. The remaining axioms are 'more or less optional' at the algebraic level. He expects them to become crucial once one works concretely ('travail sur pièces') with a given atelier defining a 'contrée' (region or space; continued on the next page). The next page adds a methodological choice: the basic primitive is the *figure*, not the point-set ('figure ensembliste'), the 'multiplicity' or the 'locus'/point. Point-sets and multiplicities are to be treated as special figures. Each figure F has three associated objects: a part F~ of a multiplicity M, a set-theoretic figure Mulomb(F) ('big multi-shadow'), and its support Omb(F) ('big shadow'). In modern terms, he is building a point-free, lattice-theoretic axiomatics of tame figures. It is analogous to an o-minimal structure or a Boolean algebra of semialgebraic/PL sets, but with figures taken as primary objects carrying more than their underlying point set. Algebraic axioms come first; dimension, connectivity, acyclicity, regularity, cell and sphere recognition and complexes are layered on afterwards.
errors: No mathematical claims are made on this page, so there is nothing to check. It is a programmatic outline.
Minor grammatical slip in the original: 'devront considérés' (missing 'être').

ideas.what: An axiomatic 'algebra of figures' / 'atelier' as the foundation of tame topology: purely algebraic axioms first, with topological, geometric and combinatorial axioms layered on later
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic tame topology; closest modern analogues are o-minimal structures, Boolean algebras of definable (semialgebraic, subanalytic, PL) sets, and mereotopology / point-free topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tame topology programme: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984). Its realisation via o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s), van den Dries' book 1998
ideas.where_published: Only the programme appears in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6; the 'atelier' axiomatics At1–At7 is unpublished

ideas.what: Stratification of the axioms: a core set At1–At7 for geometric-topological meaning, plus 'optional' axioms that become crucial when working with a specific atelier defining a 'contrée'
ideas.modern_name: Core axioms versus additional structure (cf. o-minimal axioms versus cell decomposition and triangulation theorems)

ideas.what: Figures, rather than point-sets or points, as the primitive notion; point-sets and multiplicities treated as special figures, with 'shadow'/'multi-shadow' functors to underlying sets (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Point-free / mereological approach to geometry; figures as objects carrying more than their support (akin to constructible functions or sets with multiplicity)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Point-free topology: Whitehead, de Laguna; locales: Ehresmann, Isbell, Johnstone

missed.claim: Grothendieck began a point-free, algebraic axiomatisation of tame topology ('ateliers' with axioms At1–At7). Topological regularity, balls and spheres, and complexes were to be added later as further layers. This axiomatics was never published or developed by others; the field went the model-theoretic, point-set route of o-minimality instead.
missed.quote: Je récapitule les données et axiomes d'une "algèbre des figures", ou "atelier". Il s'agit pour l'instant d'axiomes purement "algébriques"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers an alternative foundation for tame geometry in which figures, possibly with multiplicities, are primary. This could connect o-minimality with point-free topology and with constructible-function and Euler-calculus formalisms, and could support an intrinsic, recognition-theoretic treatment of balls and spheres inside a tame category.

missed.claim: The planned layering, from algebraic axioms to topological axioms (dimension/density, connectedness, acyclicity), then geometric axioms (regularity, topological balls and spheres), then combinatorial axioms (complexes), anticipates an axiomatic route to triangulation and cell-decomposition theorems. In o-minimality these are instead derived from first-order definability.
missed.quote: régularité topologique, boules et sphères topologiques d'une algèbre de figures ... la notion de complexe
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Comparing the two might show which features of tame topology are purely lattice-theoretic and which need definability.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is programmatic and contains no results. Its existence as a dated (June 1986) third draft of an axiomatic 'atelier' theory of tame figures is, however, a notable unpublished detail beyond the Esquisse sketch, and it was not pursued in the literature.
transcription_corrections: The first listed topological property looks more like 'dimension' than 'densité': '(dimension, connexité, acyclicité)' — uncertain.
'axiomes "tirés par un"' is doubtful; the handwriting is unclear (perhaps a phrase like 'de premier rang' or 'niveau un'). It should be flagged as illegible rather than given as 'tirés par un'.
The top-right annotation reads roughly 'q mention p. 23, 50-58, 59 (110-113)', where 50-58 appears struck or overwritten; 'Ch VII' is in the boxed corner.
'devront considérés' is as written by Grothendieck (missing 'être').
